Also, determine the channel where each user has posted the most words, picking the one that comes first alphabetically in case of a tie. Return a list of tuples containing the user name, their total word count, and their most active channel, sorted alphabetically by user name. Example: Input [("Alice", "general", 10), ("Bob", "help", 20), ("Alice", "help", 15)] output [("Alice", 25, "help"), ("Bob", 20, "help")].

title: Manufacturing Defect Analyzer
spec: Create a function `process(measurements)` to identify faulty parts. Input is a list of tuples containing a machine identifier, a timestamp, and a numeric part size. Calculate the average part size for each machine. Identify all sizes that deviate from the machine average by more than twenty percent. Extract the timestamps of these defective parts. Return a list of tuples where each tuple pairs a machine identifier with a sorted list of timestamps corresponding to its defective parts, sorted by the machine identifier. Example: Input [("M1", 1, 100), ("M1", 2, 105), ("M1", 3, 50)] output [("M1", [3])].

title: Garage Parking Allocator
spec: Write `allocate(vehicles)` to assign parking spots. Input is a list of parking requests where each request is a tuple containing a vehicle owner name and the vehicle size given as a number. The garage has three levels, each with a maximum capacity of five vehicles. Vehicles with a size less than four go to the first level, sizes four to six go to the second level, and sizes greater than six go to the third level. If a level is full, the vehicle is turned away. Process the requests in order and return a list of three lists, representing the first, second, and third levels respectively, containing the names of the parked vehicle owners. Example: Input [("Alice", 3), ("Bob", 5), ("Charlie", 7), ("Dave", 2)] output [["Alice", "Dave"], ["Bob"], ["Charlie"]].

title: Potluck Dish Tracker
spec: Implement `organize(commitments)` to evaluate dinner plans. Input is a list of tuples containing a guest name and the category of the dish they are bringing, such as appetizer, main, or dessert. Tally the number of dishes in each category. A successful potluck requires at least two appetizers, two mains, and one dessert, so determine which categories are falling short of their requirement. Compile a list of these deficient categories, sorted alphabetically, and a list of all unique guest names in alphabetical order. Return a tuple containing the list of deficient categories and the list of guest names. Example: Input [("John", "appetizer"), ("Jane", "dessert")] output (["appetizer", "main"], ["Jane", "John"]).

title: Spelling Bee Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(attempts)` for a competition. Input is a list of tuples containing a contestant name, the word attempted, and a boolean indicating if it was spelled correctly. Correctly spelling a word earns points equal to the length of the word, while incorrect spellings deduct one point. Find the contestant with the highest total score, breaking ties by selecting the name that comes first alphabetically. Return a tuple containing the winning contestant name and their score. Example: Input [("Eva", "cat", True), ("Sam", "elephant", False)] output ("Eva", 3).

title: Daily Habit Tracker
spec: Create `calculate(records)` to find consistency streaks. Input is a list of tuples detailing a user name, a habit name, and a day number when the habit was completed. For each user and habit combination, sort the completed days and calculate the longest streak of consecutive days the habit was completed. Find the highest streak achieved by each user across all their habits. Return a list of tuples pairing the user name with their highest streak number, sorted alphabetically by user name. Example: Input [("Leo", "run", 1), ("Leo", "run", 2), ("Leo", "read", 5)] output [("Leo", 2)].

title: Support Ticket Router
spec: Implement `route(tickets)` to assign workloads. Input is a list of tuples containing a ticket identifier, the required skill, and a priority number. There are three support agents: the first handles billing, the second handles technical, and the third handles general inquiries. Assign each ticket to the matching agent, sorting the tickets assigned to each agent primarily by priority in descending order, and secondarily by ticket identifier in ascending order. Return a list of three lists containing the sorted ticket identifiers for the billing, technical, and general agents respectively. Example: Input [("T1", "billing", 2), ("T2", "billing", 5), ("T3", "technical", 1)] output [["T2", "T1"], ["T3"], []].

title: Pantry Recipe Matcher
spec: Write a function `match(ingredients)` to suggest meals. Input is a list of available ingredient names as strings. Consider three standard recipes: a salad requires lettuce, tomato, and cucumber; a soup requires broth, potato, and carrot; a sandwich requires bread, cheese, and ham. For each recipe, count how many required ingredients are present in the input list. If all required ingredients for a recipe are present, it is considered possible. Return a list of names of the possible recipes, sorted alphabetically. Example: Input ["bread", "cheese", "ham", "tomato"] output ["sandwich"].

title: Ecosystem Population Tracker
spec: Create `track(observations)` to analyze wildlife balance. Input is a list of tuples containing a zone name, an animal type which is either predator or prey, and an observed count. Aggregate the total predator and total prey counts for each zone. Determine the balance status of each zone, classifying it as balanced if the prey count is at least twice the predator count but no more than five times the predator count, and unbalanced otherwise. Return a list of tuples containing the zone name and its balance status as a boolean, sorted alphabetically by zone name. Example: Input [("North", "predator", 10), ("North", "prey", 30), ("South", "predator", 5), ("South", "prey", 5)] output [("North", True), ("South", False)].

title: Survey Demographic Analyzer
spec: Implement `analyze(responses)` to find top ratings. Input is a list of tuples containing a demographic group name, a question identifier, and a numeric rating from one to five. For each demographic group, calculate the average rating across all questions to identify the group with the highest overall average rating. For that specific top group, find the question identifier that received the highest average rating, resolving any ties alphabetically by group name or question identifier. Return a tuple containing the top group name and its top question identifier. Example: Input [("Teens", "Q1", 5), ("Teens", "Q2", 3), ("Adults", "Q1", 4)] output ("Teens", "Q1").

title: Pet Shelter Inventory
spec: Write `manage(arrivals)` to report on shelter animals. Input is a list of tuples containing an animal species, an age in months, and a boolean indicating if it is healthy. Filter out the animals that are not healthy and group the remaining healthy animals by species. For each species, calculate the average age of the healthy animals. Sort the species by their average age in ascending order and return a list of tuples pairing the species name with its average age rounded to the nearest whole number. Example: Input [("Dog", 12, True), ("Dog", 24, False), ("Cat", 6, True)] output [("Cat", 6), ("Dog", 12)].

title: City Temperature Streaks
spec: Create `analyze(temperatures)` to find warming trends. Input is a list of tuples containing a city name and a daily temperature reading in chronological order. Group the temperature readings by city, maintaining their chronological order. For each city, find the longest consecutive sequence of days where the temperature strictly increased from the previous day. Record the length of this longest warming streak for each city and return a list of tuples containing the city name and its maximum warming streak length, sorted alphabetically by city name. Example: Input [("Paris", 10), ("Paris", 12), ("Paris", 11), ("Rome", 20), ("Rome", 22)] output [("Paris", 2), ("Rome", 2)].

title: Study Group Scheduler
spec: Implement `schedule(commitments)` to find common free time. Input is a list of tuples containing a student name, a start hour, and an end hour for their existing classes. The school day runs from hour nine to hour seventeen. Determine the busy hours for each student, where a student is busy during any hour that overlaps with their existing classes. Find the hours where all students are completely free and return a list of these free hours sorted in ascending order. Example: Input [("Dan", 9, 11), ("Dan", 13, 15), ("Eve", 10, 12)] output [12, 15, 16].

title: Vending Machine Change
spec: Write a function `vend(transactions)` to process purchases. Input is a list of tuples containing an item price and the amount tendered by the customer. The machine starts with ten coins each of quarters, dimes, and nickels, valued at twenty five, ten, and five cents respectively. For each transaction, calculate the change due and dispense it using the largest possible coins first, deducting them from the machine inventory. If the machine cannot provide exact change for a transaction, reject it and provide zero change. Return a list of tuples representing the change given for each transaction, formatted as a count of quarters, dimes, and nickels. Example: Input [(75, 100), (45, 50)] output [(1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1)].

title: Book Reading Progress
spec: Create `track(logs)` to monitor reading completions. Input is a list of tuples containing a reader name, a book title, and a chapter number read. Aggregate the unique chapters read by each reader for each book. A book is considered finished if the reader has read chapters one through five inclusive. Compile a list of book titles that each reader has finished and return a list of tuples pairing the reader name with a sorted list of finished book titles, sorted alphabetically by reader name. Example: Input [("Mia", "Dune", 1), ("Mia", "Dune", 2), ("Mia", "Dune", 3), ("Mia", "Dune", 4), ("Mia", "Dune", 5)] output [("Mia", ["Dune"])].

title: Adventure Map Router
spec: Implement `navigate(paths)` to find a goal in a maze. Input is a list of tuples representing bidirectional connections between rooms, containing the first room name and the second room name. Build a representation of the map from the connections and determine the shortest path from the start room to the treasure room, counting the number of connections. If there are multiple paths of the same shortest length, any valid path length is fine, and if the treasure room cannot be reached, the length is zero. Return the integer length of the shortest path. Example: Input [("start", "hall"), ("hall", "treasure")] output 2.

title: Volunteer Award Assigner
spec: Write `assign(shifts)` to reward volunteers. Input is a list of tuples containing a volunteer name and the number of hours worked in a single shift. Sum the total hours worked by each volunteer. Assign a gold award to volunteers with more than fifty hours, a silver award to those with more than twenty hours, and a bronze award to those with more than five hours. Volunteers with five hours or fewer receive no award. Return a list of tuples containing the volunteer name and their award string, sorted alphabetically by volunteer name, excluding those with no award. Example: Input [("Tom", 30), ("Ann", 6), ("Roy", 2)] output [("Ann", "bronze"), ("Tom", "silver")].

title: Race Age Brackets
spec: Create a function `bracket(results)` to determine race winners. Input is a list of tuples containing a runner name, their age, and their completion time in minutes. Categorize runners into three age brackets: those under twenty go to the youth bracket, those twenty to thirty nine go to the open bracket, and those forty and over go to the masters bracket. For each bracket, identify the runner with the fastest completion time, picking the one whose name comes first alphabetically in case of a tie. Return a list of three strings representing the names of the fastest runners in the youth, open, and masters brackets respectively, using an empty string if a bracket has no runners. Example: Input [("Zoe", 18, 25), ("Max", 30, 20), ("Leo", 45, 22)] output ["Zoe", "Max", "Leo"].

title: Space Debris Collision
spec: Implement `detect(objects)` to find dangerous proximities. Input is a list of tuples containing a debris identifier, an x coordinate, and a y coordinate. Calculate the straight line distance between every unique pair of debris objects. Identify pairs that are closer than five units apart and create a list of tuples containing the identifiers of the colliding pairs. Ensure the first identifier in each pair is alphabetically before the second, and sort the final list of pairs alphabetically by the first identifier, then by the second. Example: Input [("D1", 0, 0), ("D2", 3, 4), ("D3", 10, 10)] output [("D1", "D2")].

title: Subscription Revenue Calculator
spec: Write `calculate(events)` to process billing changes. Input is a list of tuples containing a user name, a subscription plan name, and an action which is either subscribe or cancel. Track the active subscription plan for each user based on the chronological sequence of events. The basic plan costs ten dollars, the pro plan costs twenty dollars, and the elite plan costs fifty dollars. Calculate the total monthly revenue by summing the costs of the currently active plans for all users and return the total revenue as an integer. Example: Input [("Ivy", "pro", "subscribe"), ("Ivy", "pro", "cancel"), ("Jon", "basic", "subscribe")] output 10.

title: Wardrobe Outfit Suggester
spec: Create a function `suggest(clothing)` to match clothes. Input is a list of tuples containing a clothing item name, its type which is either top or bottom, and its color. Separate the clothing into tops and bottoms and create all possible outfits consisting of one top and one bottom. Filter out outfits where the top and bottom are the exact same color. Compile a list of valid outfits, represented as a tuple of the top name and the bottom name, and sort the list alphabetically by the top name, then by the bottom name. Return the sorted list of valid outfits. Example: Input [("shirt", "top", "red"), ("pants", "bottom", "blue"), ("jeans", "bottom", "red")] output [("shirt", "pants")].

title: Elevator Stop Sequence
spec: Implement `sequence(requests)` to route a lift. Input is a list of tuples containing a passenger name, their starting floor, and their destination floor. The elevator starts at floor zero. It moves upwards to collect and drop off all passengers heading to a higher floor, then it moves downwards to handle passengers heading to a lower floor. Compile an ordered list of floors the elevator must stop at, where a floor is a stop if a passenger gets on or off there. Remove consecutive duplicate stops and return the final list of stopped floors. Example: Input [("Sam", 1, 4), ("Lee", 2, 5), ("Kim", 6, 3)] output [1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 3].

title: Pharmacy Expiration Tracker
spec: Write `check(medications)` to find old inventory. Input is a list of tuples containing a medication name, a department, and the days until it expires. Group the medications by their department. For each department, filter out medications that have more than three days until expiration, and sort the remaining medications by the days until expiration in ascending order. Compile a list of tuples pairing the department name with a list of the medication names that are expiring soon, and sort the final list alphabetically by department name. Example: Input [("Aspirin", "general", 2), ("Vitamins", "general", 10), ("Antibiotic", "restricted", 1)] output [("general", ["Aspirin"]), ("restricted", ["Antibiotic"])].

title: Tool Rental Assessor
spec: Create a function `assess(returns)` to calculate charges. Input is a list of tuples containing a customer name, a tool name, and the number of days the tool was kept. The standard rental period is fourteen days. For every day a tool is kept past the rental period, a late fee of two dollars is added. Calculate the total late fee for each customer across all their returned tools. Identify customers who have a total late fee exceeding twenty dollars and return a list of tuples containing the customer name and their total late fee, sorted by the fee amount in descending order, for those exceeding the threshold. Example: Input [("Rob", "Hammer", 20), ("Rob", "Drill", 20), ("Sue", "Saw", 15)] output [("Rob", 24)].

title: Sailboat Regatta Timings
spec: Write a module to manage a sailboat regatta. Provide a class that initializes separate trackers: a dictionary mapping boat names to their total race times, a list of strings for disqualified boats, and a list of integers for all recorded times. Add a method to record a race result, taking a boat name and an integer time. Add a method to disqualify a boat by name. Add a method that returns the names of all valid boats as a list of strings. Add a method to return the names of all disqualified boats as a list of strings. Add a method that returns the top three times as a list of integers. Add a standalone helper function that takes a text block of race logs separated by semicolons and returns a list of strings for each record. Add another standalone helper function that parses a single record string and returns a tuple containing the boat name and its time. Provide the main entry function `evaluate(log)` that takes a single text string, uses the helpers to split and parse it, feeds the records into the class, and returns the winning boat name as a string. Example input: windward, five; leeward, six. Example output: windward.

title: Farm Crop Yields
spec: Create a module to track harvest yields across different fields. Define a state class that initializes a dictionary mapping field names to total harvested weight, a list of strings for fields that need fertilizer, and a list of integers for all individual harvest weights recorded. Provide a method to log a harvest taking a field name and weight. Provide a method to mark a field as needing fertilizer. Add a method that extracts all field names as a list of strings. Add a method that returns the top three harvest weights as a list of integers. Add a method that returns the names of fields needing fertilizer as a list of strings. Include a standalone helper function to split a newline-separated string of harvest data into a list of strings. Include another helper function that extracts the field name and weight from a single line, returning them as a tuple. Finally, write the entry function `process(data)` that takes a single string of all harvest records, populates the state class, and returns the name of the field with the highest total yield. Example input: north, ten; south, twenty. Example output: south.

title: Historical Artifact Eras
spec: Write a tool to categorize discovered archaeological artifacts. Build a class that stores state: a dictionary mapping era names to artifact counts, a list of strings for artifacts that require restoration, and a list of integers representing the ages of all found items. Add a method to register an artifact, taking the era and age. Add a method to flag an artifact name for restoration. Include a method that returns all known eras as a list of strings. Include a method that outputs all recorded ages as a list of integers. Add a method that returns the names of artifacts needing restoration as a list of strings. Write a standalone helper function that takes a comma-separated text of discoveries and returns a list of strings. Write a second helper function that parses one discovery string into a tuple containing the era name and the artifact age. Implement the entry function `catalog(records)` that takes a text string of all discoveries, uses the helpers to parse them into the class, and returns the most common era as a string. Example input: bronze, three thousand; iron, two thousand. Example output: bronze.

title: Choir Voice Sections
spec: Develop a module for organizing a choir's voice sections. Create a class that tracks members with a dictionary mapping voice parts to member counts, a list of strings for members who are absent, and a list of integers for the vocal ranges of members. Add a method to add a member taking their voice part and range. Add a method to mark a member absent by name. Provide a method that returns all voice parts as a list of strings. Provide a method that returns the names of all absent members as a list of strings. Add a method that returns all vocal ranges as a list of integers. Create a standalone helper function that splits a semicolon-separated string of roster data into a list of strings. Create another helper function that processes a single roster entry and returns a tuple of the voice part and range. The entry function `organize(roster)` should take a single string of roster data, populate the tracking class, and return the voice part with the most members. Example input: soprano, two; alto, one. Example output: soprano.

title: Craft Fair Booth Assignments
spec: Write a script to manage booth assignments at a local craft fair. Design a class that initializes a dictionary mapping craft categories to booth counts, a list of strings for vendors needing electricity, and a list of integers for the square footage of assigned booths. Include a method to assign a booth taking the category and size. Include a method to register a vendor for electricity by name. Add a method that returns all categories as a list of strings. Add a method to return all booth sizes as a list of integers. Add a method that returns the names of vendors needing electricity as a list of strings. Write a standalone helper function that divides a text block of applications into a list of strings based on newlines. Write a helper function that evaluates a single application string and returns a tuple with the category and size. Finally, provide the entry function `assign(applications)` that accepts a string of all applications, registers them in the class, and returns the category with the highest number of booths. Example input: pottery, ten; knitting, twelve. Example output: knitting.

title: Bird Feeder Visits
spec: Build a program to analyze backyard bird sightings. Create a class that initializes a dictionary mapping bird species to visit counts, a list of strings for rare species observed, and a list of integers for the duration of visits in minutes. Add a method to log a visit taking the species and duration. Add a method to flag a species as rare. Include a method that returns all observed species as a list of strings. Include a method that outputs all rare species as a list of strings. Include a method to return all visit durations as a list of integers. Write a standalone helper function that splits a comma-separated log into a list of strings. Write another helper function that processes a single observation string to return a tuple of the species and duration. The entry function `analyze(log)` should take a text string of sightings, process them using the class and helpers, and return the most frequent species as a string. Example input: cardinal, five; bluejay, three. Example output: cardinal.

title: Mayoral Campaign Donations
spec: Write a system to track political campaign contributions. Define a stateful class that maintains a dictionary mapping donor regions to total funds, a list of strings for donors who requested refunds, and a list of integers representing all individual donation amounts. Provide a method to record a donation using the region and amount. Provide a method to log a refund request by donor name. Add a method that retrieves all donor regions as a list of strings. Add a method that retrieves the names of refund requestors as a list of strings. Add a method that returns the top five donation amounts as a list of integers. Create a standalone helper function to split a semicolon-separated text of contributions into a list of strings. Create a second helper function to parse a single contribution string into a tuple of region and amount. Provide the entry function `audit(contributions)` that takes the full text, utilizes the helpers and class, and returns the region with the highest total funds. Example input: north, fifty; south, hundred. Example output: south.

title: Sculpture Garden Layout
spec: Develop a module to plan placements in a sculpture garden. Create a class that holds a dictionary mapping artist names to the number of sculptures, a list of strings for sculptures needing special lighting, and a list of integers for the weights of the sculptures. Add a method to place a sculpture taking the artist name and weight. Add a method to mark a sculpture for special lighting. Provide a method to retrieve all artist names as a list of strings. Provide a method to get the names of sculptures needing lighting as a list of strings. Provide a method to return all weights as a list of integers. Write a standalone helper function that divides a newline-separated string of placements into a list of strings. Write another helper function that turns a single placement string into a tuple of artist name and weight. The entry function `plan(placements)` takes a string of all records, populates the garden class, and returns the artist with the most sculptures. Example input: smith, two hundred; jones, one fifty. Example output: smith.

title: Comic Book Collection
spec: Write a utility to manage a vintage comic book collection. Implement a tracking class that sets up a dictionary mapping publisher names to issue counts, a list of strings for comics in mint condition, and a list of integers for the publication years of the issues. Add a method to add an issue taking the publisher and year. Add a method to tag a comic title as mint condition. Include a method that returns all publishers as a list of strings. Include a method that returns mint condition titles as a list of strings. Include a method that lists all publication years as a list of integers. Create a standalone helper function that splits a semicolon-separated text of inventory into a list of strings. Create a helper function that parses an inventory string to return a tuple of publisher and year. The entry function `inventory(comics)` receives the full text, orchestrates the class and helpers, and returns the publisher with the most issues. Example input: marvel, sixty; dc, seventy. Example output: dc.

title: Pediatric Growth Percentiles
spec: Create a medical tracking module for pediatric growth. Design a class that initializes a dictionary mapping patient names to their latest percentile, a list of strings for patients requiring dietary review, and a list of integers for all recorded heights. Add a method to update a patient's percentile taking their name and height. Add a method to flag a patient for dietary review. Provide a method that outputs all patient names as a list of strings. Provide a method that returns all flagged patients as a list of strings. Provide a method that retrieves all recorded heights as a list of integers. Write a standalone helper function that breaks a comma-separated string of clinical data into a list of strings. Write a helper function that parses a single data string into a tuple containing the patient name and height. Finally, the entry function `evaluate(records)` takes a string of records, manages the state, and returns the patient with the highest height. Example input: alice, forty; bob, thirty. Example output: alice.

title: Antique Furniture Appraisal
spec: Write a program to summarize antique furniture appraisals. Build a class that stores a dictionary mapping furniture types to total estimated values, a list of strings for items needing restoration, and a list of integers for the ages of the pieces. Include a method to appraise an item taking the type and value. Include a method to mark an item for restoration. Add a method that returns all furniture types as a list of strings. Add a method that returns items needing restoration as a list of strings. Add a method to return all piece ages as a list of integers. Create a standalone helper function that splits a text block of appraisals into a list of strings. Create another helper function that converts a single appraisal string into a tuple of the furniture type and value. Implement the entry function `appraise(items)` that takes the text of all items, uses the helpers and class, and returns the furniture type with the highest total value. Example input: chair, fifty; table, hundred. Example output: table.

title: Poetry Syllable Counter
spec: Develop a module to analyze the structure of poems. Create a class that tracks poem data using a dictionary mapping stanza themes to line counts, a list of strings for lines with imperfect rhymes, and a list of integers for the syllable counts of each line. Add a method to process a line taking its theme and syllable count. Add a method to log an imperfect rhyme. Provide a method that retrieves all themes as a list of strings. Provide a method that lists imperfect rhymes as a list of strings. Provide a method that returns all syllable counts as a list of integers. Write a standalone helper function that takes a semicolon-separated text of poem lines and returns a list of strings. Write a helper function that parses one line string into a tuple of theme and syllable count. The entry function `analyze(poem)` takes the full poem text, applies the logic, and returns the theme with the most lines. Example input: nature, ten; love, eight. Example output: nature.

title: Ski Resort Lift Tickets
spec: Write a tracking tool for ski resort lift usage. Define a class that maintains a dictionary mapping lift names to passenger counts, a list of strings for passes that are expired, and a list of integers for the scan times. Include a method to record a scan taking the lift name and scan time. Include a method to log an expired pass by holder name. Add a method that lists all lift names as a list of strings. Add a method that returns expired pass holders as a list of strings. Add a method that returns all scan times as a list of integers. title: Language School Class Sizes

title: Perfume Scent Profiles
spec: Develop a module to classify perfume formulations. title: Ocean Buoy Temperatures
spec: Write a script to aggregate oceanic temperature readings. title: Boarding Kennel Feeding

title: Lighthouse Flash Patterns

title: Seed Bank Inventory

title: Fossil Discovery Locations

title: Amateur Radio Logbook
spec: Create a utility for amateur radio operators to log contacts. title: Pottery Kiln Firings
spec: Build a program to monitor pottery kiln firing cycles. Define a state class that initializes a dictionary mapping glaze types to piece counts, a list of strings for pieces that cracked, and a list of integers for the firing temperatures. title: Beekeeping Hive Health
spec: Write a module to assess the health of bee colonies. Create a class that stores a dictionary mapping hive names to honey yields, a list of strings for hives needing mite treatments, and a list of integers for the bee populations. title: Astronomy Telescope Viewing
spec: Develop a script to manage observations at a public observatory. title: Bakery Bread Inventory

title: Movie Theater Seating Optimizer
spec: Write a function `seat(reservations, rows)` that assigns group reservations to theater rows. The reservations input is a list of tuples containing the group name string and the number of people integer. The rows input is a list of integers representing the capacity of each row in order from front to back. A group must sit together in the same row, taking the first available row from the front that can fit them. If a group cannot fit in any single row, they are skipped and not seated. Return a list of lists of strings, where each inner list contains the names of the groups seated in that corresponding row. Example: seat([("smith", 3), ("jones", 2), ("davis", 4)], [4, 5]) returns [["smith"], ["jones"]].

title: Dungeon Loot Distributor
spec: Create a function `distribute(party, loot)` that allocates dropped items to adventurers based on their class. The party input is a list of tuples where each tuple has the character name string and their class name string. The loot input is a list of tuples containing the item name string and the intended class string. Iterate through the loot and assign each item to a character of the matching class. If multiple characters share the required class, the items should be dealt out to them in round-robin fashion, using an internal tracker of how many items each eligible character has received to ensure fairness. Return a list of tuples pairing each character name with a list of the item names they received, in the same order as the party list. Example: distribute([("gimli", "fighter"), ("legolas", "archer")], [("axe", "fighter"), ("bow", "archer"), ("sword", "fighter")]) returns [("gimli", ["axe", "sword"]), ("legolas", ["bow"])].

title: Spacecraft Cargo Balancer
spec: Develop a function `load(items, holds)` that assigns cargo to spacecraft holds to maximize space utilization. The items input is a list of tuples containing the cargo identifier string and its weight integer. The holds input is a list of integers representing the maximum weight capacities of available cargo holds. Sort the items by weight from heaviest to lightest, then place each item into the first hold that can accommodate its weight. Return a list of lists of strings, representing the cargo identifiers assigned to each hold in the order the holds were provided. Example: load([("food", 5), ("water", 10), ("oxygen", 7)], [15, 10]) returns [["water", "food"], ["oxygen"]].

title: Tournament Bracket Generator
spec: Implement `bracket(players)` to create matchups for a single elimination tournament. The players input is a list of tuples pairing a player name string with their ranking integer, where a lower number means a better rank. Sort the players by their ranking and pair the best ranked player with the worst ranked player, the second best with the second worst, and so on. If there is an odd number of players, the best ranked player gets a bye and is paired with a placeholder string representing no opponent. Return a list of tuples, each containing the two string names of the players facing off in the first round. Example: bracket([("alice", 1), ("bob", 3), ("charlie", 2)]) returns [("alice", "none"), ("charlie", "bob")].

title: Train Carriage Sorter
spec: Write `shunt(carriages)` to reorganize train carriages so that those carrying the same type of freight are adjacent. The carriages input is a list of strings representing the freight types in their initial sequence. Find all unique freight types and group the carriages by type, ordering the groups based on the first appearance of each type in the original sequence. Return a tuple containing the newly ordered list of carriages and an integer representing the number of carriages that changed their position index compared to the original sequence. Example: shunt(["coal", "wheat", "coal", "iron"]) returns (["coal", "coal", "wheat", "iron"], 2).

title: Historical Battle Simulator
spec: Design `clash(attackers, defenders)` to simulate combat between two armies. Both inputs are lists of tuples, where each tuple contains a unit name string, an attack power integer, and a health integer. In each round, the first unit in the attackers list strikes the first unit in the defenders list, reducing its health by the attack power. If the defender survives, it strikes back at the attacker in the same manner. Any unit whose health falls to zero or below is removed from its army list. The battle continues until one army has no units left. Return a tuple containing a string indicating the winning army, either attackers or defenders, and a list of tuples representing the surviving units and their remaining health. Example: clash([("spearman", 3, 10)], [("militia", 1, 5)]) returns ("attackers", [("spearman", 9)]).

title: Theme Park Fastpass Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(requests, capacities)` to allocate priority access at a theme park. The requests input is a list of tuples with a visitor name string, a preferred ride string, and an integer hour slot. The capacities input is a list of tuples specifying a ride string, an hour slot integer, and the maximum number of fastpasses allowed integer. Process the requests in the order they appear, granting a fastpass if the corresponding ride and hour slot has not yet reached its maximum capacity. Return a list of tuples containing the visitor name, the ride, and the hour, representing the successfully granted fastpasses. Example: schedule([("tom", "coaster", 10), ("sue", "coaster", 10)], [("coaster", 10, 1)]) returns [("tom", "coaster", 10)].

title: Baggage Carousel Assigner
spec: Implement `assign(flights, carousels)` to direct arriving luggage to baggage carousels. The flights input is a list of tuples with a flight code string and an integer representing the number of bags. The carousels input is a list of tuples with a carousel identifier string and its maximum bag capacity integer. For each flight, assign it to the carousel with the largest remaining capacity that can hold all the bags. If multiple carousels have the same remaining capacity, choose the one appearing first in the carousels list. If no carousel can hold the bags, ignore the flight. Return a list of tuples pairing the flight code with the assigned carousel identifier. Example: assign([("flight one", 50), ("flight two", 60)], [("carousel a", 100), ("carousel b", 100)]) returns [("flight one", "carousel a"), ("flight two", "carousel b")].

title: Magic Gathering Deck Validator
spec: Create a function `validate(deck, rules)` to check if a trading card deck meets format restrictions. The deck input is a list of strings representing card names. The rules input is a list of tuples containing a card name string and an integer for the maximum allowed copies of that card. First, count the occurrences of each card in the deck. Then, compare these counts against the rules. If any card exceeds its maximum allowed copies, record a violation. Return a list of tuples, each containing the name of the rule-breaking card and the integer number of excess copies, sorted alphabetically by card name. Example: validate(["goblin", "goblin", "goblin", "dragon"], [("goblin", 2)]) returns [("goblin", 1)].

title: Zoo Enclosure Planner
spec: Develop `enclose(animals)` to group animals safely into habitats. The animals input is a list of tuples where each tuple contains an animal name string and a list of string names of other animals they are hostile towards. Iterate through the animals and place each into the first available enclosure where they have no hostilities with any current occupant, and no current occupant has a hostility towards them. If no existing enclosure is safe, create a new one. Return a list of lists of strings, where each inner list represents the names of animals sharing an enclosure. Example: enclose([("lion", ["zebra"]), ("zebra", ["lion"]), ("elephant", [])]) returns [["lion", "elephant"], ["zebra"]].

title: Pirate Treasure Splitter
spec: Write `split(treasures, crew)` to divide loot among pirate crew members. Sort the treasures in descending order of value, then distribute each item to the pirate who currently has the smallest total share value. If multiple pirates have the same smallest total, give it to the one who received their first item earliest. Return a list of lists of integers, showing the values of the treasures assigned to each pirate, ordered by pirate index. Example: split([10, 8, 7, 5], 2) returns [[10, 5], [8, 7]].

title: Art Gallery Wall Curator
spec: Implement `hang(paintings, walls)` to arrange artwork in a gallery. The paintings input is a list of tuples containing a painting name string, a theme string, and a width integer. The walls input is a list of integers representing the maximum width each wall can hold. Group the paintings by theme, then within each theme, sort them by width from narrowest to widest. Process the themes alphabetically, hanging each painting on the first wall that has enough remaining width. If a painting cannot fit on any wall, skip it. Return a list of lists of strings, where each inner list contains the names of paintings hung on a specific wall. Example: hang([("starry", "sky", 5), ("sunflower", "nature", 4)], [6, 6]) returns [["sunflower"], ["starry"]].

title: Camping Gear Allocator
spec: Create `equip(campers, gear)` to distribute outdoor equipment based on preferences. The gear input is a list of strings representing the available equipment items. Iterate through the campers in multiple rounds. In each round, grant every camper the highest available item on their preference list that they have not yet received. Stop when no camper can be assigned any more gear. Return a list of tuples pairing each camper name with a list of the gear they received. Example: equip([("dan", ["tent", "stove"]), ("amy", ["tent", "lamp"])], ["tent", "stove", "lamp"]) returns [("dan", ["tent", "stove"]), ("amy", ["lamp"])].

title: Orchard Harvest Forecaster
spec: Design `forecast(trees)` to estimate future fruit yields. The trees input is a list of tuples containing a tree identifier string, a fruit type string, and a list of integers representing the yield in kilograms over consecutive past years. For each tree, predict the next year yield by calculating the integer average of its past yields, rounded down. Then, aggregate these predictions by fruit type. Return a list of tuples pairing each fruit type string with the total predicted yield integer for that fruit, sorted alphabetically by fruit type.
